_readme: 26 West, 600 W 26th St - the 2008 student block on the north side of W 26th St between Rio Grande and Nueces - as js/slopes-apartments.js draws it. OSM way 187381178 carries this outline as building=apartments and nothing else: no name, no address, no height, no levels. What this file draws is the L that the polygon is - the five-storey bar along W 26th St and the wing that turns north up Nueces - not the whole 26 West site, whose garage, courtyard ring and north wing are separate polygons in the snapshot. The building is one massing repeated: a two-storey masonry base that alternates red brick and pale rusticated stone in about 9 m blocks, three storeys of stucco above it in the same 9 m blocks in cream, terracotta and pale blue, a white cornice and a flat white roof - with a projecting 4 m pier under a grey hipped cap every 17 m along 26th St, a bigger cap turning the Nueces corner, and - the thing that reads first on the real building - a nearly black loggia slot cut full height into the wall beside every pier. Metres in the footprint's oriented bounding box (js/westcampus.js obbOf): L=123.8, W=82.6, +u at bearing 95.1 deg, so u=0 is the WEST end towards Rio Grande, +u runs east along W 26th St, v=0 is the SOUTH (W 26th St) edge and +v runs north. Every number carries a _src naming a key in `sources`, or says derived or unknown. Read docs/apartments.md for the schema.

footprint._src: S1 verbatim. In (u,v) the ten vertices are (33.0,20.2) (0.0,20.1) (0.0,0.0) (123.7,0.0) (123.8,76.5) (117.1,76.5) (117.1,82.7) (103.4,82.7) (103.3,20.2) - a bar 123.7 x 20.15 m along W 26th St with a 20.5 m wide wing running 62 m north up Nueces and stepping 6.2 m further east at its north end.

_frame_src: obbOf(ring) as the generator computes it: L=123.8, W=82.6, +u at bearing 95.1 deg. +v is 90 deg counter-clockwise from +u in (east, north), so it is very nearly north and v=0 is the W 26th St edge (S10). Confirm against the boot console line.

levels._src: FIVE storeys - S4 and S5 say so independently, and S7 shows five window rows on the corner tower. Measured in S7 at that tower, whose base, cornice and hip apex are all visible against the sidewalk: base to cornice 126.7 px and the apex 18.3 px above that, which at 0.1156 m per pixel with the 62 deg tilt taken out is 16.59 m to the cornice and 18.99 m to the apex. S1's 19.2 m is a surface-model maximum and lands on the hips, not on the parapet - so the parapet top is entered at 16.60 and the roof plane 0.80 below it at 15.80. Floor to floor in the upper storeys measures 22.5 px = 2.95 m in the same frame (four window rows over 135 px in S7's blue block); 2.90 is entered so that four upper storeys and one taller ground floor close on 15.80 exactly, which makes the ground floor 4.20 m. Uncertainty plus or minus 0.15 m a storey.
levels._heights_src: base 7.10 is the level-3 floor line: the masonry base is two storeys. S7 puts the bottom edge of the blue stucco 64 px above the sidewalk on the 26th St face = 8.4 m, and S8 puts the brick's top a little lower on the blocks either side of the entrance; the level-3 floor line at 7.10 is inside that spread and is where a two-storey base has to stop. Uncertainty plus or minus 0.8 m. cornice 15.40 is the white band under the parapet, set so the top row of windows (sill 12.9 + 0.85, head + 1.50 = 15.25) still fits under it.

colours._src: Day hex; golden and night follow js/westcampus.js's ramp(). Every hex is a k-means cluster centre of a named crop of a named capture, entered a step down from the sunlit reading because the generator lights the face itself.

cream._src: S8 crop (420,415)-(490,468), one ivory block: 72.3 % #ecebe1, 25.3 % #d8dad4. k-means of a named crop of S8's frame c_south_mid (the 26th St elevation at 230 m, 0.121 m per pixel measured off the 3.0 m window bay), 2026-09-05 look-fix pass. The first pass entered #e2ded1 and the render read grey-tan beside a reference that is nearly white; entered one step under the sunlit cluster instead.

terracotta._src: S8 crop (650,420)-(720,485), one sunlit peach block: 68.7 % #d6b99b. k-means of a named crop of S8's frame c_south_mid (the 26th St elevation at 230 m, 0.121 m per pixel measured off the 3.0 m window bay), 2026-09-05 look-fix pass. It reads apricot in this imagery, not red.

blue._src: S8 crop (320,425)-(390,500), the big blue block: 73.2 % #b1c5d3. k-means of a named crop of S8's frame c_south_mid (the 26th St elevation at 230 m, 0.121 m per pixel measured off the 3.0 m window bay), 2026-09-05 look-fix pass. The first pass's #adc4d3 was within a step of it; entered at the measurement.

brick._src: S8 crop (420,480)-(490,520), two storeys of the base under an ivory block: 34.7 % #b8a192 and 29.6 % #aa8c7c, the sunlit and shaded halves of the same brick (the third cluster, 35.7 % #dfd9ce, is the pale banding). k-means of a named crop of S8's frame c_south_mid (the 26th St elevation at 230 m, 0.121 m per pixel measured off the 3.0 m window bay), 2026-09-05 look-fix pass. Entered between them. The first pass's #9f8270 was darker than either and made the base read as mud.

stone._src: S8 crop (290,480)-(330,520), the pale rusticated stretch of the base: 66.5 % #dbd3c6. k-means of a named crop of S8's frame c_south_mid (the 26th St elevation at 230 m, 0.121 m per pixel measured off the 3.0 m window bay), 2026-09-05 look-fix pass, entered a step down.

trim._src: the white window surrounds, the cornice band and the parapet coping. S7's roof-membrane crop clusters to #dddeda and the cornice reads brighter than it in every oblique, so this is entered above the membrane.

hip._src: S8 crop (585,400)-(620,418), one grey hipped cap: 64.8 % #999ea1 sunlit, 31.9 % #787e83 in shade. k-means of a named crop of S8's frame c_south_mid (the 26th St elevation at 230 m, 0.121 m per pixel measured off the 3.0 m window bay), 2026-09-05 look-fix pass, entered just under the sunlit face.

roof._src: S8 crop (370,375)-(470,390), the flat white membrane: 82.1 % #e0e1dd. k-means of a named crop of S8's frame c_south_mid (the 26th St elevation at 230 m, 0.121 m per pixel measured off the 3.0 m window bay), 2026-09-05 look-fix pass, entered a step down.

glass._src: the punched windows are the darkest cells in every facade cluster: #3d3b3b and #4e4b48 in S7's blue-wall crop, #5e666f where there is sky in them. Entered between the two - a dark window with a little sky in it, which is what the reference shows.

rail._src: the balcony rails read as a pale grey line in S8 and S9 c_southwest; not separately sampled - entered between the trim white and the hip grey.

mech._src: S6 nadir: the roof condensers are a mid grey a shade darker than the hips.

loggia._src: S8 crop (553,430)-(570,505), the full-height recess between two piers: 44.6 % #2d2625 (the 28.6 % #dad6ca beside it is the pale slab edge at each floor and the 26.7 % #72675f is the recess's own return). k-means of a named crop of S8's frame c_south_mid (the 26th St elevation at 230 m, 0.121 m per pixel measured off the 3.0 m window bay), 2026-09-05 look-fix pass. This is the darkest thing on the elevation and the first pass had no tone for it at all.

slotDark._src: derived: the openings inside the recess, entered a step under `loggia` so the reveal still cuts a shadow line inside a dark wall.

skins._src: One rule per treatment; every count comes from a module, never a hard-coded number. The building has two wall treatments and a cornice, and both walls use the SAME two modules: a 9.0 m colour block and a 3.0 m window bay.

masonry._src: The two-storey base. It is not one material: it alternates red brick and pale rusticated stone in blocks the same width as the stucco blocks above. Reading S9 c_southwest left to right along the 26th St front the base goes stone, brick, brick, stone, brick, and S8 gives the same alternation across the entrance. macro [2,1] on a 3.55 m course makes the tone constant over both storeys of one block; bond 0 keeps the block edges vertical, which is what a masonry change line is. runMax 2 lets two blocks share a material, which the reference does. Two window rows fall in this band, at the 0.0 and 4.2 m floor lines. LOOK-FIX: window re-measured with the stucco one, 1.30 x 1.70 on a 0.90 m sill.

stucco._src: The three stucco storeys. THE RULE: full-height vertical colour blocks, one tone each, on a 9.0 m module, in cream, terracotta and pale blue. The block width was measured in S8 as 77 and 97 px across two adjacent blocks at 0.099 m per pixel = 7.6 and 9.6 m, with the wall nearly perpendicular to the camera so there is almost no foreshortening; 9.0 m is three window bays. The window bay is 3.0 m: S7's blue block measures 5.8 m and carries two window columns. macro [3,1] on a 2.90 m course is exactly the three storeys of this band, so the tone runs the block's full height, which is what the reference does at every block edge. The weights are the share of blocks of each tone counted along the 26th St and Nueces elevations in S8, S9 c_southwest and S9 c_east: 11 cream, 8 terracotta, 6 blue out of 25. The window is 1.35 x 1.50 m on a 0.85 m sill - S7 measures the opening at 1.06 x 1.31 m and the white surround adds about 0.15 m a side. reveal 0.22 is deeper than the app's 0.12 default because these are punched openings in a thick stucco wall and the shadow line inside them is the strongest thing on the reference's elevation. LOOK-FIX: the window was 1.35 x 1.50 and read square beside a reference whose openings are plainly portrait. Measured again in S8 at 0.121 m per pixel (the 3.0 m bay is 25 px, which is what sets that scale): the opening with its white surround is 10 by 14 px = 1.21 x 1.69 m. Entered 1.25 x 1.75.

cornice._src: the white band between the top of the stucco and the roof, under the parapet. Continuous on every elevation in S7, S8 and S9 c_east.

loggia._src: THE RECESSED LOGGIA, and it is the strongest thing on this building's elevation. Beside each projecting pier the wall opens into a slot that runs the whole height of the building, from the pavement to the cornice, and it is nearly black: S8 clusters it at #2d2625 against #ecebe1 for the ivory beside it. Pale floor slabs cross it at every level - the 28.6 % #dad6ca cluster in the same crop - which is what `floorLine` draws. Width measured in S8 at x = 553..571, 18 px at 0.121 m per pixel = 2.18 m; entered at 2.6 m because the slot's own shaded returns eat a pixel a side. The first pass drew these as 0.32 m PROJECTING balconies because the generator only projects; `overrides` turns out to do it properly - a region of a wall wearing other bands - so the recess is a recess.

blocks._src: S1's ring, the u 0..123.7 by v 0..20.15 part: the bar that fronts W 26th St for the block's whole width, Rio Grande to Nueces. Read off the rectified nadir (S6), where the roof is one plane at one height for the whole length with the courtyard light well behind it at v 21..25.
blocks._parapet_src: 0.80 m: the white upstand between the top of the cornice band and the roof plane, 7 px in S7 at 0.1156 m per pixel with the 62 deg tilt taken out. It runs right round in every oblique.

roofItems._src: S6 nadir: this wing's roof carries condensers in two loose rows along its whole length, about 1.2 x 2.4 m each.

LOOK-FIX. The first pass drew each cap as a 7.2 x 6.8 m three-step box standing 5.6 m back on the roof, and beside the reference it read as a mechanical penthouse, not a roof. Measured again in S8 with the 3.0 m window bay as the scale (25 px a bay, 0.121 m per pixel): the caps at x = 490..535 and 855..900 are 45 px = 5.4 m wide and the pier under each is 30 to 38 px = 3.6 to 4.6 m, so the cap oversails its pier by about half a metre a side. Entered 5.2 m square, straddling the wall from v = -1.0 (0.4 m proud of the pier's face) to v = 4.2, in five steps instead of three so the silhouette is a pyramid rather than a ziggurat. Apex still 19.0 m - S1's 19.2 m surface-model maximum lands here, not on the parapet. The u pitch is still the nadir's 17.2 m least-squares fit; S8 shows the real rhythm is irregular, which the rule cannot express - see todo 7.
S7: the corner of W 26th and Nueces carries a bigger cap over a chamfered corner bay - 6.6 m, one step wider than the rest. Drawn square; see todo 2.

overrides._src: The seven recessed loggia slots on the W 26th St front, one beside each pier, at u = pier - 5.0 to pier - 2.4. The region reaches v = -1 .. 1 so it catches this rectangle's v0 wall and nothing else. See skins.loggia.

blocks._src: S1's ring, the u 103.3..123.8 by v 20.15..82.65 arm with its 6.2 m step at the north end: the wing that fronts Nueces St. Entered as a polygon so the step is real. Edge 0 is its south edge and stands on the bar.

faces._src: 0 is the south edge at v = 20.15 and stands on the bar, so it is not drawn. 1 is the Nueces elevation and carries the balcony bays. 5 is the west edge on the light well; 2, 3 and 4 are the north end's step. They all wear the same stack - S9 c_east shows the same base, the same colour blocks and the same cornice on Nueces as on 26th.

roofItems._src: S6 nadir: two rows of condensers up this wing.

The Nueces caps, the same 5.2 m square five-step rule as the 26th St ones, straddling the wall at u = 123.8 (so u = 119.6 .. 124.8). v = 28.5, 41.0, 53.5, 66.0 - the nadir's two measured caps at 41.0 and 53.5 with that 12.5 m pitch continued over the wing.

overrides._src: The four loggia slots on the Nueces elevation, one beside each pier, at v = pier - 5.0 to pier - 2.4. S9 c_east shows the same dark full-height recess here as S8 does on 26th. The region's u = 123.0 .. 124.5 catches only face 1, the wall at u = 123.8.

todo: 1. DONE in the look-fix: the recessed balconies are recesses now. `overrides` - a region of a wall wearing other bands - does what a projecting balcony could not, so skins.loggia draws the slot and the generator needs nothing new. The projecting `balcony` block has been deleted.
2. The W 26th and Nueces corner tower is chamfered at 45 degrees in S7 and is drawn square. A polygon plan can do it, but its two returns then need per-edge faces that the rectangle keys cannot name.

3. The hipped caps are five-step grey ziggurats because the generator has no pitched roof. At the app's oblique camera (about 0.3 m per pixel) each step is under a pixel and reads as a hip; at walking height it will read as steps.

4. The leasing entrance on 26th St - a recessed opening with a canopy and a dark 26 WEST sign band over it, visible in S8 at about x = 720..765 - is not drawn; it wears the base's punched windows instead. It is left out because the frame gives its screen position and not its u, and a sign in the wrong bay is worse than no sign.
5. u = 6.3 and 109.5 on the 26th St front, and v = 28.5 and 66.0 on Nueces, are the pier rule's prediction rather than measurements. A ground photograph of either street would settle them.

6. The west end wall at u = 0 is a party wall against the next polygon of the same block and wears the ordinary skin. Nobody can see it, and it is not worth a face of its own until that neighbour is authored too.

7. The pier pitch is entered as a uniform 17.2 m from the nadir's least-squares fit, but S8's elevation shows the real rhythm is irregular - three consecutive caps 26.6, 10.6 and 33.2 m apart, and one of them twice the width of the others. A per-pier list of measured u values would beat the rule; it needs a rectified elevation, not a rectified plan.
